How the series fits together

Architecture & distribution

Creative MCP is a series of independent MCP implementations created by Zach Shallbetter. Each tool lives in its own repository and release cycle. They share one website, one Homebrew tap and one catalogue, with a series installer planned.

Getting startedContentMCP APICLI & configArchitectureInDesignIllustratorPhotoshopAfter EffectsPremiereSuite

The series today

Each implementation is a separate project with its own language, licence and release process. They share no runtime, API or process. A client can load several at once, but moving files between them is a handoff you manage.

How releases reach you

Every tool is published through its own ecosystem first (npm for Adobe MCP, Cargo for Blender MCP), then gets a formula in the Creative MCP Homebrew tap. Homebrew installs the runtime the tool needs, so you don't have to set up Node.js or Rust yourself.

brew tap zachshallbetter/tap
brew trust zachshallbetter/tap        # Homebrew 7+: trust a third-party tap once
brew install zachshallbetter/tap/adobe-mcp
brew install --HEAD zachshallbetter/tap/blender-mcp

Each formula runs a real MCP initialize check as its test. Update with brew upgrade. For Blender MCP, use brew upgrade --fetch-HEAD blender-mcp until it has tagged releases.

Planned: one installer for the series

Status: Planned. The installer described here does not exist yet. Until they ship, use the per-tool installs above or the setup builder.

A browser can't see which apps you have installed, so the series will get a small local installer that can. creative-mcp setup will:

  • detect installed creative apps (on macOS by bundle ID, for example com.adobe.Photoshop and org.blenderfoundation.blender) and MCP clients (commands on your PATH and their config files)
  • show a checklist with the matching tools pre-selected, and let you change it
  • install your choices with Homebrew where available, or the tool's own method otherwise
  • register each tool with the clients you choose, showing every config change first and backing up the file
  • start each server once to confirm it answers MCP initialize

It will also have list, doctor, update, add and remove commands, and --yes, --dry-run and --json flags. Detection runs only on your machine and sends nothing anywhere.

brew install zachshallbetter/tap/creative-mcp   # planned
creative-mcp setup                             # planned

One catalogue for every tool

Status: Draft. The first version of the catalogue is published at creativemcp.com/registry.json, with a JSON Schema, and validated on every change in the creative-mcp repository. Nothing reads it yet; the pages below are still written by hand.

Every place that lists tools (these docs, the setup builder, llms.txt, the installer and the tap) will read this one versioned catalogue. Each entry records the tool's repository, licence, author, capability status, install methods, server commands, the apps it targets and how to detect them, and the clients it supports. Adding a tool to the series then means adding one entry.

Adding a tool to the series

  1. Create the repository with a README, licence files, contribution guide and tagged releases.
  2. Publish a package and add a formula to the tap with a working test.
  3. Add the entry to registry/registry.json, with detection rules checked on a real machine (mark unchecked ones "verified": false).
  4. Add the implementation guide to these docs.
  5. Record capability status honestly: only Validated means the workflow ran in the real app and its result was checked.

See the contribution guide for review expectations.
